record.original_question: If a complex polynomial P of degree n>1 shares at least one root with each of its derivatives P^(k) for k=1,...,n-1, must P be of the form b(z-a)^n for some complex numbers a and nonzero b?

evidence.quote: Problem 30 (Casas-Alvero's conjecture). If a complex polynomial P of degree n > 1 shares roots with all its derivatives, P^(k), k = 1, 2, ..., n - 1, then there exist two complex numbers, a and b != 0, such that P(z) = b(z - a)^n.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $P(z) \in \mathbb{C}[z]$ be a polynomial of degree $n > 1$, and for each $k = 1, 2, \dots, n-1$ let $P^{(k)}$ denote the $k$-th formal derivative of $P$. Suppose that for every $k \in \{1, 2, \dots, n-1\}$ the polynomials $P$ and $P^{(k)}$ have a common root in $\mathbb{C}$ (equivalently, $\gcd(P, P^{(k)})$ is non-constant). Prove or disprove: there must exist $a \in \mathbb{C}$ and $b \in \mathbb{C} \setminus \{0\}$ such that
$$P(z) = b(z-a)^n.$$
artifact.status_search_result: The Casas-Alvero conjecture has been verified for many families of degrees (e.g., prime powers and certain composite cases) for years. A January 2025 arXiv preprint by Soham Ghosh ("Proof of the Casas-Alvero conjecture", arXiv:2501.09272) claims a complete proof in characteristic zero using Koszul homology, but as of May 2026 this proof has not yet been confirmed as published/refereed in a journal of record, so the conjecture's full resolution remains not universally accepted. Other 2023–2025 works (Schaub–Spivakovsky, etc.) provide further partial results.

status_evidence.title: Proof of the Casas-Alvero conjecture (arXiv:2501.09272)
status_evidence.snippet: Soham Ghosh proves the Casas-Alvero conjecture for polynomials of degree d≥3 over any characteristic 0 field using Koszul homology.
status_evidence.claim: A 2025 preprint claims a complete proof of the conjecture in characteristic zero.

status_evidence.title: Casas-Alvero conjecture - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: The Casas-Alvero conjecture is an open problem proposed by Eduardo Casas-Alvero in 2001, verified for various families of degrees.
status_evidence.claim: Historically the conjecture has been known only in special cases.

status_evidence.title: On the Casas-Alvero Conjecture (Journal of Commutative Algebra, 2025)
status_evidence.snippet: Schaub and Spivakovsky establish partial results related to resultants attached to the conjecture.
status_evidence.claim: Recent published work continues to provide partial progress.
